target: Orang tua saya tinggal jauh dari sini.
english: My parents live far from here.
tip: orang tua = parents (lit. old people): orang tua saya = my parents.

target: Kantor pos ada di sebelah kanan.
english: The post office is on the right side.
tip: ada isn't 'have' here – it marks that something is somewhere: kantor pos ada di sebelah kanan = the post office is (exists) on the right. Indonesian drops 'is', but location keeps ada.

target: Kantor saya jauh dari rumah.
english: My office is far from home.
tip: jauh dari = far from; dekat dengan = near to.

target: Saya naik bus ke kantor setiap hari.
english: I take the bus to the office every day.
tip: naik + vehicle = take/ride: naik bus = take the bus.

target: Tas saya ada di atas meja.
english: My bag is on the table.
tip: di + position word: di atas meja = on (top of) the table.

target: Kunci ada di dalam tas hitam itu.
english: The key is inside that black bag.
tip: Descriptions follow the noun and 'that' comes last: tas hitam itu = bag-black-that. English order is reversed – itu always closes the phrase.

target: Mobil saya parkir di depan gedung.
english: My car is parked in front of the building.
tip: The owner follows the thing owned: mobil saya = car-my. No 's and no 'of' – just put the possessor right after the noun it belongs to.

target: Rapat mulai jam sembilan pagi.
english: The meeting starts at nine in the morning.
tip: jam goes before the number for clock time: jam sembilan = nine o'clock. Flip it to sembilan jam and it means nine hours – the order decides which.

target: Dari sini ke bandara berapa lama?
english: How long from here to the airport?
tip: No do/does shuffle in questions: berapa lama (how long) just sits where the answer would – Dari sini ke bandara berapa lama? The word order never moves.

target: Di mana halte bus terdekat?
english: Where is the nearest bus stop?
tip: ter- + adjective = the most: terdekat = the nearest, from dekat (near).

target: Kantor kami ada di lantai lima.
english: Our office is on the fifth floor.
tip: kami means 'we, not including you': kantor kami = our office, but not yours. If the listener is part of the group, Indonesian switches to kita.

target: Saya sudah mengirim email ke bos.
english: I have already sent an email to the boss.
tip: Verbs never change for tense – sudah does the work: sudah mengirim = have already sent. Drop sudah and the same sentence could be present or future.

target: Jangan lupa bawa laptop ke rapat.
english: Don't forget to bring a laptop to the meeting.
tip: jangan = don't (command): Jangan lupa! = Don't forget!

target: Dia sedang bekerja dari rumah hari ini.
english: He is working from home today.
tip: dia is both 'he' and 'she' – Indonesian pronouns ignore gender. Dia sedang bekerja could describe anyone; only context tells you who.

target: Orang yang duduk di sana itu teman saya.
english: The person who is sitting over there is my friend.
tip: yang links a noun to its description: orang yang duduk = the person who is sitting.

target: Baju yang kamu beli kemarin bagus sekali.
english: The shirt that you bought yesterday is really nice.
tip: yang also links a noun to what someone did to it: baju yang kamu beli = the shirt that you bought.

target: Makanan yang dia masak selalu enak.
english: The food that she cooks is always delicious.
tip: The verb after yang can keep its own subject: yang dia masak = that she cooks.

target: Bus yang ke bandara berangkat jam enam.
english: The bus that goes to the airport leaves at six.
tip: No verb for 'goes' here – yang ke is enough: bus yang ke bandara = the bus that goes to the airport.

target: Harga di pasar lebih murah daripada di toko.
english: Prices at the market are cheaper than at the shop.
tip: daripada is only for comparing; 'from' a place is plain dari.

target: Saya lebih suka teh daripada kopi.
english: I prefer tea to coffee.
tip: lebih suka X daripada Y = prefer X to Y: lebih suka teh = prefer tea.

target: Mana yang lebih murah, taksi atau ojek?
english: Which is cheaper, a taxi or a motorbike taxi?
tip: mana yang lebih ... asks 'which one is more': mana yang lebih murah? = which is cheaper?

target: Dia karyawan paling rajin di kantor kami.
english: He is the most diligent employee in our office.
tip: paling before an adjective makes 'the most': paling rajin = the most diligent.

target: Kamar ini yang paling murah di hotel ini.
english: This room is the cheapest one in this hotel.
tip: yang here means 'the one': Kamar ini yang paling murah = this room is the one that's cheapest. Without yang it's just 'this room is cheapest'.

target: Stasiun mana yang paling dekat dari sini?
english: Which station is the closest from here?
tip: mana after a noun asks 'which': stasiun mana = which station.

target: Kakak saya sekarang setinggi ayah saya.
english: My older sibling is now as tall as my father.
tip: se- + adjective means 'as ... as': setinggi ayah = as tall as father.

target: Bahasa Indonesia tidak sesulit bahasa Jepang.
english: Indonesian is not as difficult as Japanese.
tip: tidak se- + adjective = 'not as ... as': tidak sesulit = not as hard as.

target: Tolong tutup pintu itu, di luar dingin.
english: Please close that door, it is cold outside.
tip: tolong before a verb makes a polite request: tolong tutup pintu = please close the door.

target: Tolong bicara pelan-pelan, saya masih belajar.
english: Please speak slowly, I am still learning.
tip: Doubling an adjective makes a gentle adverb: pelan-pelan = slowly.

target: Tolong tunggu sebentar, saya ambil uang dulu.
english: Please wait a moment, I will get money first.
tip: dulu after a verb means 'first, before anything else': saya ambil uang dulu.

target: Tolong panggil taksi untuk kami, ya.
english: Please call a taxi for us, okay?
tip: In requests the bare root is normal: tolong panggil, not tolong memanggil.
